about.title: Colma Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Colma is a small city, but its residents and visitors still rely daily on cars, machinery, tools, appliances, and consumer goods that are supposed to work safely. When one of those products fails — a defective part, a poorly designed tool, or a warning label that never mentioned a real risk — the person hurt is often left facing medical bills and confusion about who should be held accountable. California's strict liability rules mean an injured person doesn't have to prove a manufacturer was careless, only that the product itself was defective and caused harm. That can include the maker, a distributor, or even the local retailer who sold it. If you were injured by a faulty product anywhere in Colma or nearby San Mateo County, we can review what happened and explain your options. There's no obligation, and we only get paid if you recover.

Lacerations or amputations from defective tools or machinery
Head or eye injuries from parts that shatter or malfunction
Poisoning or chemical burns from mislabeled products
Crush injuries from unstable furniture or appliances
Injuries from vehicle parts or airbags that fail to perform

whyChoose.title: Why Product Liability Cases Work Differently

items.title: Strict Liability Can Apply
items.desc: California often lets an injured person recover by showing a product was defective and caused harm, without having to prove the manufacturer was negligent.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the store that sold the product can potentially share liability under California law.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Keeping the defective item, its packaging, and any related paperwork can be important evidence, and our team can advise on how to protect it.

items.question: I was hurt by a product I bought outside of Colma but use here — does that matter?
items.answer: Not usually. What matters is that you were injured in California and the product was defective, not exactly where it was purchased. We can look at the specifics of your situation and explain how California law applies.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Often no. California's strict liability approach generally focuses on whether the product itself was defective in design, manufacturing, or warnings, and whether that defect caused your injury. This can make these claims different from typical negligence cases.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to keep it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, along with any packaging, instructions, or receipts. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away, since it may serve as key evidence for our team in reviewing your case.

items.question: Is there a cost to get a case review?
items.answer: No. Our initial consultation is free, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover money for your injury.
